tasks.short: Consult users and engineers on change requirements

steps.what: Submit the change or purchase need
Read the current system before the meeting
Hold the requirements meeting with users
Draft the requirements note from the fields

loop.input: request fields and the note template
loop.output: note with each need tagged to a field
loop.check: Every need line cites a request field or is marked as said in the meeting
loop.stop: One draft; drop any line with no field and no meeting mark
loop.why_not_simpler: Spoken needs do not match a fixed mail-merge, and a template cannot invent a field

steps.what: Sign the requirements version
File the signed requirements note

tasks.design: Users, site administrators and engineers submit a change or a purchase on a {WORKFLOW} form with a system id and a business need. A bounded draft in {DOCS} turns those fields into a requirements note. The telecommunications specialist still holds the meeting and signs one version. Nothing is bought from an unsigned note.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requirements lived in meeting notes and mail, so a draft could not tell a wish from an agreed need.
tasks.enabler_now: The request form and the inventory can share one system id, so each need can be tied to a field.
tasks.still_hard: People disagree in the room about what the business will pay for, and that is not a form.
tasks.human_edge: The specialist decides which stated needs are in scope and which stay as wishes.

ambition.what: Sign a requirements version for each proposed change, not only in the yearly plan

tasks.altitude: Less time rewriting notes after the meeting. The specialist can refuse a purchase that has no signed requirements version.

reach.task: Draw a change from the signed requirements note
reach.learn: Which needs are signed and which are still only wishes

evidence.claim: In a mid-size firm this task is a meeting. The record afterwards is the part that can be structured.
Digest [S3] says a document product can fill metadata from a prompt, and the vendor warns the fill can be wrong, so the specialist still checks every requirement field.

assumptions: Focal role is the telecommunications specialist. The task ends when a signed requirements version is filed. Buying the item is a later task.

Input contract: request id, system id, site, business need, requester, requested date. Producer is the system user, a site administrator or an engineer. If the form is empty the specialist types the same fields from the meeting and marks the row manual.
Use the document store's own templates before custom code. The meeting itself is not replaced by a form.
unknowns: Who may sign when the specialist is absent.
Whether an external engineer may see the inventory.
research_questions: What share of purchases last quarter had no written requirements?
How often does the meeting overturn the submitted need?

already_counted.description: Meeting time stays with the specialist
Signature judgement on the requirements note

incremental.description: Update the requirements template when a new site type appears
Requesters correct fields the form rejects

approvals.approved_version: requirements note version signed in this meeting
the same signed requirements note version

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes most needs still arrive as free talk, so the form is thin and the specialist rewrites the note. The high case assumes the form is used but every meeting and every signature still happen. The purchase itself is not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Test hardware and software for compatibility

steps.what: Open the test cases for this version
Run the compatibility cases on the bench
Store the instrument log as rows
Decide pass, fail or a site limit
File the signed test result

tasks.design: A standard script on the {OPS_SYSTEM} writes a log row for each case: device id, software version, result code and site. A {BI} view shows fails against the acceptance rule. The telecommunications specialist decides pass, fail or a site limit for that version. The script does not write to production gear. Putting the version into service is a later task.
tasks.previous_blocker: Test notes were handwritten or pasted into mail, so a later test could not line up with the same case id.
tasks.enabler_now: The test instrument and the inventory can share a device id, so each result can be a row instead of a paragraph.
tasks.still_hard: A new combination can pass the script and still be wrong for this site. That call stays with the specialist.
tasks.human_edge: The specialist decides whether a failed case is acceptable here and whether a retest is required.

ambition.what: Retest after each software version, not only before a large cutover

tasks.altitude: Less time copying results into a document. The specialist can refuse a version that has no signed test result.

reach.task: Retest a control the specialist marked incompatible
reach.learn: Which versions passed and which cases are still open

evidence.claim: Compatibility tests in a mid-size firm are bench work plus a log. Only repeated cases suit a fixed script.
Digest [S28] reports a coding agent that deleted a production database despite instructions, so a test script must not write to production gear.

assumptions: Focal role is the telecommunications specialist. The task runs from a planned test to a signed result. Production cutover is a later task.

Input contract: test id, device id, software version, case id, site, acceptance rule. Producer is the test script, or the specialist when the script has no case id. Cases with no device id stay on a manual bench list.
Configure the instrument's own log export before custom code. The in-person share is the bench, not a workshop. No unattended write to production gear.
unknowns: Which devices expose a log export versus a screen only.
Who may sign a failed case that the site will accept.
research_questions: What share of tests repeat a case id already in the script?
How often is the first result overturned?

already_counted.description: Hands-on bench time stays with the specialist
Pass or fail judgement stays with the specialist

incremental.description: Add new case ids to the test script after repeated versions
Engineers correct device ids the log rejects

approvals.approved_version: test result signed for this test id and software version

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes most devices have no log export, so the specialist still types results and the script rarely fires. The high case assumes logs are clean but every pass or fail stays manual. Production cutover is not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Assess facility needs for telecommunications changes

steps.what: Book the site visit with facilities
Walk the site and fill the checklist
Compare checklist counts with the inventory
Draft the needs note from the rows

loop.output: needs note whose counts cite a room id
loop.check: Every count in the note equals a checklist or inventory field
loop.stop: Leave a blank and stop that room if a count has no field
loop.why_not_simpler: The reason a room is a problem is not a fixed lookup

steps.what: Decide which gaps are real needs
File the signed needs note

tasks.design: A site checklist on {WORKFLOW} records room, device count, conduit spare and user count. The {BI} view compares those counts with the inventory. A bounded note in {DOCS} drafts the gap list from those rows only. The telecommunications specialist walks the site and signs which gaps are real needs.
tasks.previous_blocker: Needs were prose in visit notes, so two sites could not be compared and a draft would invent counts.
tasks.enabler_now: A checklist and the inventory can share a room id and a device type, so a gap is a missing or short row.
tasks.still_hard: Whether a cramped room should be rebuilt is a facilities decision, not a count.
tasks.human_edge: The specialist decides which gaps are worth a project and which the site can live with.

ambition.what: Reassess a site after a move, not only when a renovation is already funded

tasks.altitude: Less time rewriting visit notes. The specialist can refuse a needs statement whose counts are not on the checklist.

reach.task: Plan the room works the specialist marked as needed
reach.learn: Which rooms are short of conduit or devices and which are accepted

evidence.claim: A facilities assessment in a mid-size firm is a site walk plus a count. The hard part is which shortages matter, not the formatting.
Digest [S3] says a document product can fill metadata from a prompt, and the vendor warns the fill can be wrong, so every count in the needs note must match a checklist field.

assumptions: Focal role is the telecommunications specialist. The task ends at a signed needs note. Designing the new system is a later task.

Input contract: site id, room id, device type, device count, conduit spare, user count, visit date. Producer is the specialist on the walk, or facilities staff when they submit the form. A room with no count is left blank, not guessed.
Use the checklist and the inventory export before custom code. Walking the site stays manual. The in-person share is that walk.
unknowns: Whether some sites forbid a shared checklist on a phone.
Who owns conduit records, facilities or telecommunications.
research_questions: What share of rooms has no device count on the inventory?
How often does the signed need differ from the first checklist?

already_counted.description: Site-walk time stays with the specialist
Needs decision stays with the specialist

incremental.description: Add checklist fields when a new room type appears
Facilities staff resubmit rooms the form rejects

approvals.approved_version: needs note signed for this site visit

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes checklist use is patchy, so the specialist still writes the note from memory. The high case assumes counts are clean but every site walk and every needs decision stays manual. The renovation project is not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Document support problems, fixes and installations

steps.what: Capture the problem, action and status
Suggest a category from the symptom

loop.input: symptom text and the category list
loop.output: one category id or a blank
loop.check: The category id is on the approved list
loop.stop: If none fits, leave the category blank and stop
loop.why_not_simpler: Free-text symptoms do not match a keyword table reliably

steps.what: Confirm the category and the action
Copy the completed installation row
Draft a knowledge line from the record

loop.input: confirmed action field and the knowledge template
loop.output: one line that cites the ticket id
loop.check: The line cites the ticket id and adds no step that is not in the action field
loop.stop: One draft; discard it if the action field is empty
loop.why_not_simpler: The wording varies, but a template cannot keep the words inside the action field

steps.what: Accept or drop the knowledge line

tasks.design: Support work is entered once on the {HELPDESK}: system id, symptom, action taken, resolution status and installation id. A bounded pass suggests a category for the telecommunications specialist to confirm. Completed installation rows copy from the work order into the same record. A knowledge line in {DOCS} is drafted only from a confirmed record, and the specialist accepts or drops it.
tasks.previous_blocker: The same fix was written in mail, in a notebook and again in a ticket, and the fields did not match.
tasks.enabler_now: A ticket can require a system id and a status, so the record is the work, not a second document.
tasks.still_hard: A messy symptom still needs a person to say what was actually done, and some installs have no work order id.
tasks.human_edge: The specialist confirms the category and the corrective action before the record closes.

ambition.what: Small-site staff can read a confirmed fix without calling the specialist again

tasks.altitude: The second write-up goes away. The specialist can refuse to close a record that has no system id or no action.

reach.task: Reuse a confirmed fix instead of opening a new diagnosis
reach.learn: Which symptoms already have a confirmed action and which are still open

evidence.claim: Digest [S1] and [S2] say a service desk can suggest a ticket category and draft a knowledge item for a person to review.
Digest [S22] says security logging must stay necessary and proportionate. A support record should store system id, action and status, not the content of a call.
Documenting a fix in a mid-size firm is still a second write-up after the call. The diagnosis itself is a different task.

assumptions: Focal role is the telecommunications specialist. The task is the record of support and of completed installations, not the diagnosis conversation.

Input contract: ticket id, system id, symptom text, action taken, resolution status, installation id, owner. Producer is the specialist or the colleague who did the work. A row with no system id and no installation id is not closed by rule.
Use the helpdesk's own required fields and category list before custom code. A knowledge line is published only after the specialist accepts it.
unknowns: Whether an installer outside the team can write the installation id.
Who may accept a knowledge line when the specialist is away.
research_questions: What share of tickets last month had no action text?
How many knowledge drafts were dropped?

already_counted.description: Confirm time on the support record stays with the specialist
Knowledge-line review stays with the specialist

incremental.description: Keep the category list aligned with new system types
Colleagues fix tickets the form rejects

approvals.approved_version: support record confirmed for this ticket id
knowledge line accepted for this ticket id

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes many closures still arrive as free-text mail, so the specialist retypes them. The high case assumes the form is used but every category and every knowledge line is still reviewed. Diagnosis time is not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The specialist keeps the requirement meetings, the site walks and the pass or fail calls, and stops retyping test logs and support records.
reach: Network architects read the signed requirements note instead of asking what was agreed.
Network operators take the filed test result and the closed support record as their queue.
skills_to_grow: Write a requirement as a field a template can check.
Record a compatibility test as a row with a device id and a result code.
Close a support record from the action taken, not from a second write-up.
role.ambitious_version: Every proposed change has a signed requirements note, a filed test result and a support record that names the system.
